slides.heading: River Sizes
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Graphs
slides.narration: Let's solve River Sizes, a medium graphs problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: In a 0/1 matrix, sizes of all 4-directionally connected groups of 1s (any order).
slides.narration: Here's the problem. In a 0 or 1 matrix, sizes of all 4-directionally connected groups of 1s (any order).

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Each river is a connected component of ones; flood-fill to measure it.
slides.narration: Each river is a connected component of ones; flood-fill to measure it.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Brute force: re-explore from every 1 → repeated work
Visited matrix + DFS/BFS → each cell once, O(w·h)
slides.narration: Exploring from every one without remembering visits repeats work. With a visited matrix, each cell is processed once, linear in the grid size.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. On an unvisited one, DFS or BFS to count its size
slides.narration: Step by step. First, scan every cell. Second, on an unvisited one, DFS or BFS to count its size. Third, mark visited cells.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We scan every cell. On an unvisited one, we start a stack-based flood fill, counting popped cells and pushing unvisited neighbouring ones, then record the size.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of w times h. Space is O of w times h.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Mark visited when pushing, not popping
slides.narration: Mark cells visited when you push them, otherwise the same cell can be pushed twice and counted twice.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Follow-up: largest island after flipping one 0 (Largest Island)
slides.narration: Union-find is an alternative. The hard follow-up flips one zero to maximise an island.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Each river is a connected component of ones; flood-fill to measure it.
slides.narration: To recap River Sizes: Each river is a connected component of ones; flood-fill to measure it. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
